# PRB-001: SSH is not reachable from the internet on a private ingress host

- **Group:** Outside view
- **Severity when it fails:** moderate
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

This result comes from stackward probe, run from another machine: it shows what the internet sees after the provider firewall, the host firewall and Docker have all had their say, which is the view NET-009 says the host audit cannot have. On a host whose ingress is a tunnel or the tailnet, a public SSH port is attack surface nobody needs: it draws constant password and key guessing, and every OpenSSH vulnerability becomes reachable. Port 22 is always tried; extra ports added on the command line count when they answer with an SSH banner. The banner is printed because it names the OpenSSH version an attacker sees. With the auto profile there are no host facts to infer the profile from, so an open port is judged as if nothing should be public (warn). On a public web or panel profile an open SSH port is reported as info.

## Verify by hand

```sh
nc -vz -w 3 <host> 22   # from another machine; add -6 for IPv6
```

## How to fix it

Make SSH work over the tailnet first, then close the public SSH rule in the host firewall and the provider firewall (see SSH and NET checks).

## What a fix can break

Closing public SSH before a private path works locks you out; keep the provider console at hand.

Run `stackward explain PRB-001` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
